metric_rationale: Response is recoded so y=1 means chose A and y=0 means chose B. The highest-validity cue is feature 0. For trials where feature 0 favors A, TTB says p(A) is the same no matter what the five lower-validity cues say; similarly, for trials where feature 0 favors B, TTB says p(A) is the same across lower-cue configurations. The metric therefore takes, within each top-cue block, the proportion of A choices on trials where the lower five cues favor A on net minus the proportion on trials where they favor B on net. TTB's expected value is 0 in both blocks, up to binomial noise. Tallying counts every cue, so it predicts more A choices when lower cues favor A and fewer when lower cues favor B; hence both differences are positive, and their average is near +1 when choices are decisive. Averaging the two top-cue blocks controls for TTB's fixed bias toward A or B and yields a scalar with small per-subject variance under TTB and a large positive value under Tallying.

This metric measures the signed behavioral sensitivity of choices to the objective tally difference: trials where option A beats option B on strictly more features (tally difference positive) versus trials where option B beats option A on strictly more features (tally difference negative). In this design, the positive and negative tally groups each contain four repeated pairs, two of which have a first discriminating cue favoring A and two favoring B. Therefore a Take The Best agent is expected to choose A at 50% in both groups, making this contrast zero on average, while a Tallying agent should choose A at a high rate in the positive group and a low rate in the negative group, producing a large positive value. Averaging across four pairs per group per subject uses 32 trials per group, stabilizing the per-subject estimate and keeping between-subject variance small.
